synopses.short: China: The Mbappé-Chairman Mao controversy explained
synopses.medium: Kylian Mbappé has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong.
synopses.long:
Kylian Mbappé has apologised for "ill-judged" comments he made about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong which led to him being dropped by several Chinese brands.

Mbappé had reportedly told French talk show The Bridge the meme "that makes me laugh the most, is the one where there's a video of a guy, I think it's a Chinese dictator..." He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao.

The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a "dictator" because of his huge influence in football.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world," Mbappé said in a statement.

The BBC's China correspondent Stephen McDonnell explains the controversy.
